subject: CAIQ submission: Branch protection narrative and PR triage workflow (artifact bundle)
messages:
From: Maya Patel <auditor@brightcap.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CAIQ request — branch protection / PR triage artifacts

Hi Sean,

As part of BrightCap's CAIQ intake we need a short narrative and a small artifact bundle that demonstrates Redwood's branch protection and pull request triage process. Specifically we'd like: 

- The branch protection rules in place (enforce PR review, required status checks, prevent force-push to protected branches)
- The PR triage workflow (labels, ownership, SLA to respond, who is authorized to merge)
- A sample PR export showing review traceability (commits, review comments, reviewer approvals)
- Evidence that CI checks are enforced (a failing pipeline blocks merge) and a list of required checks
- Any documented temporary bypass / emergency-merge process and the approvals tied to it

We prefer a single zipped artifact, but Drive links + a couple of exported logs are fine. Can you provide these materials and a short narrative by end of day Friday 4/8? Also include a contact for any technical follow-ups (who on your side we can ping about CI checks or logs).

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Compliance Manager, BrightCap

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <auditor@brightcap.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ request — branch protection / PR triage artifacts

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. I've pulled together a small bundle and a short narrative; attaching the PDFs/exports below and dropping a Drive folder with the same items for convenience. High level notes up front:

- Branch protection: we enforce branch protection on main and release/* branches. Required: 2 approvers, status checks passing (lint, unit, integration), and no deletions/force pushes. Policy is centrally managed via an org-level GitOps config.
- PR triage: triage label set (triage:high/medium/low); ownership is assigned via CODEOWNERS for service repos; on-call triage SLA is 8 business hours for triage acknowledgement, target 48 hours to first substantive review.
- CI enforcement: merges gated by required checks (see attached CSV). We intentionally run blocking integration tests in the PR pipeline; failing jobs mark the status check as failed and block the merge button in the UI.
- Emergency bypass: we have a documented emergency-merge runbook (attachment: emergency-merge-log shows examples and approvals). Bypasses require a documented post-hoc approval ticket and an approver from SRE + the service owner.

Attachments included (also in Drive): branch-protection-policy-2028-04.pdf, sample-pr-1234-export.json, ci-required-checks-2028-04.csv, emergency-merge-log-2028-02-19.csv.

Contact for follow-ups: Jordan Blake (jordan@redwood.com) — he owns GitHub/GitOps policies and can provide CI job logs if you need them.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_branch_policy
HubSpot intake record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/record/BC-12345

Let us know if you want the artifacts packaged as a signed PDF bundle for auditor upload.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Security Enablement
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <auditor@brightcap.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: CAIQ request — branch protection / PR triage artifacts

Hi Maya — adding a bit more technical context and a short policy snippet you'd find useful. (Forwarded from Sean's reply.)

Policy excerpt (org-gitops/branch-protection.yaml):
- protected_branches:
  - pattern: main
    required_approvals: 2
    required_status_checks:
      - name: ci/lint
      - name: ci/unit
      - name: ci/integration
    allow_force_pushes: false

PR triage notes:
- We use CODEOWNERS to map service areas to reviewers; automated triage label bot (labeler) applies triage:low/medium/high based on changed dirs.
- Triage assignment flow: label -> oncall rotation notified -> acknowledgement within SLA (8 business hours).
- Merge authority: only users in the 'service-owner' or 'release-admins' GitHub teams can perform merges to protected branches.

Enforcement evidence we've included:
- sample-pr-1234-export.json (includes commit SHAs, review timestamps, reviewer handles)
- ci-required-checks-2028-04.csv (list of checks that gate merges across service repos)
- emergency-merge-log-2028-02-19.csv (post-hoc approvals recorded in ticketing system)

If BrightCap needs a CSV of actual blocked-merge events over the last 90 days, we can export that (may contain internal PR metadata — we can redact as needed).

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Patel <auditor@brightcap.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Thanks Sean and Jordan — the material looks good and the snippet helps. I have one follow-up: for the CAIQ we need evidence that secrets rotation is executed on schedule for CI service accounts and an export of rotation events (redacted where appropriate). Can you provide a short ledger showing rotation timestamps for the last quarter and indicate where keys are stored (KMS provider / HSM)?

If you can add that by 4/7 EOD we'll include it in our bundle. Also confirm whether emergency bypass approvals are captured in Jira tickets with the approver signature (an export or screenshot is fine).

Best,
Maya

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <auditor@brightcap.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ request — branch protection / PR triage artifacts

Maya — attaching the secrets rotation ledger for Q1 and a short note on key custody. Quick summary:

- Rotation ledger: secrets-rotation-ledger-2028-q1.csv (columns: secret_id, environment, rotated_at_utc, rotated_by, rotation_method). We redacted secret names to IDs per our export policy.
- KMS: Redwood uses AWS KMS for customer-managed keys in our hosted offering; for private deployments customers may use their own KMS/HSM. The ledger includes a column for KMS key id (redacted) and a rotation method flag (automated cron lambda or manual vault-case).
- Emergency bypass: all emergency merges require a Jira ticket and a post-hoc approval documented in the ticket with approver email and timestamp. Emergency-merge-log-2028-02-19.csv in the bundle is an export of those ticket references and approver handles.

I'm dropping the signed ZIP to the Drive folder now; if BrightCap requires a notarized PDF we can produce one for upload.

Drive folder (updated): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_branch_policy
Jira ticket example: SEC-721 (contains a redacted approval trail).

Let me know if you need any further redactions or a PGP-signed bundle.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Security Enablement
Redwood Inference
